title: Windows' best free screenshot app just got much better at copying text off your screen
excerpt: The update is out as a pre-release for now
content_html:
Published Nov 27, 2026, 9:38 AM EST

Anvinraj Valiyathara is a technology journalist with more than 15 years of experience covering the global tech industry. He has published over 20,000 articles across outlets including GizmoChina, Croma Unboxed, MySmartPrice, Pricebaba, Playfuldroid, BGR India, Free Press Journal, and IBTimes.

He specializes in tech news, leaks, smartphones, consumer electronics, and emerging technologies and has reviewed everything from phones and tablets to wearables.

Anvinraj is known for accuracy and for turning complex technical developments into clear, accessible stories. Outside work, he's a Formula 1 fan who loves to travel.

ShareX 22.5.0 replaces Windows' built-in OCR with a local AI engine that can recognize text in over 100 languages. There's no language pack to install or language to pick. The project says the results are significantly more accurate, and the update is currently available as a pre-release.

The new engine is PaddleOCR, and text recognition still runs locally on your device. ShareX 22.5.0’s source ships with PP-OCRv6 small detection and recognition models, and the project's OCR library describes the setup as offline OCR. The two ONNX models plus their configuration files come to about 31MB, and they’re bundled in the setup and portable builds.

The old Language and Scale factor options are gone because the new models support multiple languages and no longer rely on Windows language packs. The redesigned OCR window displays a preview with recognized text outlined. Clicking a region copies its text, the mouse wheel zooms in and out of the preview, a Separate paragraphs option preserves paragraph structure, and text in captures can also be made searchable in history.

More than a new text reader

A pixel editor, a faster capture tool, and a pre-release catch

The change is aimed at people who already treat ShareX as a free replacement for several Windows tools, as well as those who regularly copy text using Windows 11's Snipping Tool. It also joins Microsoft's PowerToys Text Extractor as another local way to grab text directly from the screen.

ShareX 22.5.0 also adds a pixel editor for creating pixel art and sprite animations. It includes support for layers, an animation timeline, tilemaps, slices, and sprite sheet import and export. Region capture now opens about twice as fast, while the Ellipse region and Freehand region tools have returned. The image editor also gets an optional compact toolbar, and the project has moved to .NET 11.

The download is larger, though. The 64-bit setup weighs 160.4MB, up from 138.7MB in version 22.4.0. The portable build has also grown to 221.8MB from 200.0MB. The OCR models aren't the only reason for the increase, as the pixel editor and .NET 11 migration add to the download size. ShareX hasn't published separate hardware requirements for the new OCR engine.

The setup and portable download buttons on the ShareX website still point to the latest stable release, version 22.4.0. That means you won't get the new OCR engine by default unless you download the 22.5.0 pre-release separately, even if ShareX is already your everyday Windows screenshot app.
